s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic mucocutaneous blistering disorder with oral and skin involvement
salient_findings: Presence of bullae, erosions, and crusts on the lower lip, oral cavity, face, trunk, and extremities
Skin biopsy showing spongiosis, neutrophils, and perivascular dermatitis
key_facts: 39-year-old woman with no significant medical history
No swollen cervical and axillary lymph nodes
Small bullae, erosions, and crusts on the lower lip
Erosions with epithelized mucosa in the oral cavity
Flaccid discrete and coalesced bullae, crusts, and erosions on the face, trunk, and extremities
Normal chest, abdomen, and pelvic computed tomography
Normal gastrointestinal endoscopy and colonoscopy results
Skin biopsy revealed spongiosis and numerous neutrophils with nuclear dust in the epidermis
Superficial perivascular dermatitis with predominant infiltration of lymphocytes in the dermis
Positive immunoblotting for IgG autoantibodies to envoplakin and periplakin

differentials: Autoimmune bullous dermatosis associated with inflammatory bowel disease
per_call: Autoimmune bullous dermatosis associated with inflammatory bowel disease

shortlist.label: Paraneoplastic pemphigus
shortlist.why_kept: Positive immunoblotting for IgG autoantibodies to envoplakin and periplakin, which is characteristic of paraneoplastic pemphigus

shortlist.label: Mucous membrane pemphigoid
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic mucocutaneous blistering disorder with oral and skin involvement, consistent with mucous membrane pemphigoid

shortlist.label: Pemphigus vulgaris
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of mucocutaneous lesions and positive immunoblotting, although the lack of IgG antibodies to Dsg1 and Dsg3 makes it less likely

shortlist.label: Linear IgA bullous dermatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic blistering disorder with linear IgA deposits, although the negative direct IF results make it less likely

shortlist.label: Lichen planus pemphigoides
shortlist.why_kept: Interface dermatitis and presence of mucocutaneous lesions, although the lack of specific immunological findings makes it less likely

raw.rationale: The presence of autoantibodies to envoplakin and periplakin, as well as the clinical presentation of mucocutaneous lesions, is most consistent with paraneoplastic pemphigus.

rejected.label: Mucous membrane pemphigoid
rejected.why: Lack of deposits of IgG, IgA, and C3 at the basement membrane zone and negative indirect IF using 1-molar sodium chloride-split normal human skin

rejected.label: Pemphigus vulgaris
rejected.why: Negative chemiluminescent enzyme immunoassays for Dsg1 and Dsg3

rejected.label: Linear IgA bullous dermatosis
rejected.why: Negative direct IF for IgA deposits and lack of linear IgA deposits at the basement membrane zone

rejected.label: Lichen planus pemphigoides
rejected.why: Clinical and histopathological features do not align with lichen planus pemphigoides, and the presence of autoantibodies to envoplakin and periplakin is more specific for paraneoplastic pemphigus
